claim: Pancreatic cancer has a 5-year survival rate of only 11% and ranks fourth among tumor-related deaths in the United States.
source: As the most aggressive tumor, pancreatic cancer (PACA) has a 5-year survival rate of only 11% and ranks fourth among tumor-related deaths in the United States (Siegel et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Siegel et al., 2022

claim: 80–85% of PACA patients have progressed or metastasized at the time of detection and lost the opportunity for surgical resection.
source: Due to its insidious clinical manifestations and lack of available early detection and screening tools, 80–85% of PACA patients have progressed or metastasized at the time of detection, and lost the opportunity for surgical resection (Mizrahi et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mizrahi et al., 2020

claim: ICIs have yielded disappointing clinical results in PACA because of the complex composition and highly suppressive immune microenvironment.
source: Unfortunately, ICIs have yielded disappointing clinical results in PACA because of the complex composition and highly suppressive immune microenvironment (Bear et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bear et al., 2020

claim: The PARP inhibitor olaparib extended progression-free survival of BRCA-mutated PACA patients (3.8 months vs. 7.4 months) but did not significantly improve overall survival.
source: However, a recent study confirmed that although the PARP inhibitor olaparib extended progression-free survival of patients (3.8 months vs. 7.4 months), the overall survival (OS) was not significantly improved (Golan et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Golan et al., 2019

claim: The CD40 monoclonal antibody APX005M in combination with chemotherapy achieved a 58% response rate in advanced PACA in a phase Ib multicenter study.
source: Reassuringly, the result of a phase Ib multicenter study showed that the CD40 monoclonal antibody APX005M in combination with chemotherapy achieved a 58% response rate in advanced PACA (O'Hara et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to O'Hara et al., 2021

claim: The high inter- and intra-tumoral heterogeneity of PACA results in a wide range of outcomes even among patients at the same stage.
source: Although this provides a relatively trustworthy reference for determining whether patients will undergo surgical resection, the high inter- and intra-tumoral heterogeneity of PACA results in a wide range of outcomes even among patients at the same stage (Liu et al., 2022c).
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2022c

claim: 32 consensus prognostic genes were screened from 1280 patients across 10 multicenter cohorts.
source: Based on expression files of 1280 patients from 10 multicenter cohorts, we screened 32 consensus prognostic genes.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract with specific numbers

claim: Ten machine-learning algorithms were transformed into 76 combinations for model construction.
source: Ten machine-learning algorithms were transformed into 76 combinations, of which we selected the optimal algorithm to construct an artificial intelligence-derived prognostic signature (AIDPS) according to the average C-index in the nine testing cohorts.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract

claim: AIDPS could accurately predict the prognosis of PACA in the training cohort, nine testing cohorts, Meta-Cohort, and three external validation cohorts (290 patients).
source: The results of the training cohort, nine testing cohorts, Meta-Cohort, and three external validation cohorts (290 patients) consistently indicated that AIDPS could accurately predict the prognosis of PACA.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract with specific cohort numbers

claim: AIDPS exhibited robust and dramatically superior predictive capability after incorporating several vital clinicopathological features and 86 published signatures.
source: After incorporating several vital clinicopathological features and 86 published signatures, AIDPS exhibited robust and dramatically superior predictive capability.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract

claim: The nine-gene AIDPS could accurately stratify the prognosis in other prevalent digestive system tumors.
source: Moreover, in other prevalent digestive system tumors, the nine-gene AIDPS could still accurately stratify the prognosis.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract

claim: Patients with low AIDPS had a dismal prognosis, higher genomic alterations, and denser immune cell infiltrates and were more sensitive to immunotherapy.
source: Of note, our AIDPS had important clinical implications for PACA, and patients with low AIDPS owned a dismal prognosis, higher genomic alterations, and denser immune cell infiltrates as well as were more sensitive to immunotherapy.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract

claim: The high AIDPS group possessed observably prolonged survival.
source: Meanwhile, the high AIDPS group possessed observably prolonged survival, and panobinostat may be a potential agent for patients with high AIDPS.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract

claim: Panobinostat may be a potential agent for patients with high AIDPS.
source: Meanwhile, the high AIDPS group possessed observably prolonged survival, and panobinostat may be a potential agent for patients with high AIDPS.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract with speculative language ('may be')

claim: The combination of CoxBoost and Survival-SVM with the highest average C-index (0.675) was selected as the final model.
source: As shown in Figure 2A, the combination of CoxBoost and Survival-SVM with the highest average C-index (0.675) was selected as the final model.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 2A

claim: The high AIDPS group possessed significantly longer survival in the PACA-AU-Array training cohort (p<0.0001 in OS and p=0.012 in RFS).
source: The Kaplan–Meier curve for OS and RFS demonstrated the high AIDPS group possessed significantly longer survival in the PACA-AU-Array training cohort (p<0.0001 in OS and p=0.012 in RFS, Figure 3A and B).
evidence: Supported by Kaplan-Meier analysis with specific p-values and reference to Figure 3A and B

claim: AIDPS was an independent protective factor for OS and RFS in the PACA-AU-Array cohort (HR: 0.593 [0.504–0.697] for OS and 0.762 [0.611–0.949] for RFS, both p<0.05).
source: In addition, we further enrolled several important clinical traits for multivariate Cox analysis, and the results indicated that AIDPS was an independent protective factor for OS and RFS in the PACA-AU-Array cohort (HR: 0.593 [0.504–0.697] for OS and 0.762 [0.611–0.949] for RFS, both p<0.05, Figure 3E and F).
evidence: Supported by multivariate Cox analysis with specific hazard ratios and confidence intervals

claim: AIDPS was an independent prognostic factor for OS and RFS in the Meta-Cohort (HR: 0.603 [0.531–0.685] for OS and 0.667 [0.552–0.805] for RFS, both p<0.05).
source: Similar results were also found in the Meta-Cohort (HR: 0.603 [0.531–0.685] for OS and 0.667 [0.552–0.805] for RFS, both p<0.05, Figure 3G and H).
evidence: Supported by multivariate Cox analysis with specific hazard ratios and confidence intervals

claim: The AUCs of 1-, 2-, and 3-year OS were 0.715, 0.748, and 0.671 in the PACA-AU-Array training cohort.
source: The area under the ROC curve (AUCs) of 1-, 2-, and 3-year OS were 0.715, 0.748, and 0.671 in the PACA-AU-Array training cohort and 0.717, 0.719, and 0.719 in the Meta-Cohort (Figure 3K and L).
evidence: Supported by ROC analysis with specific AUC values

claim: The AUCs of 1-, 2-, and 3-year OS were 0.717, 0.719, and 0.719 in the Meta-Cohort.
source: The area under the ROC curve (AUCs) of 1-, 2-, and 3-year OS were 0.715, 0.748, and 0.671 in the PACA-AU-Array training cohort and 0.717, 0.719, and 0.719 in the Meta-Cohort (Figure 3K and L).
evidence: Supported by ROC analysis with specific AUC values

claim: AIDPS had significantly improved accuracy compared to common clinical traits including age, gender, race, diabetic history, TNM stage, grade, primary location, history of radiotherapy or alcohol consumption, surgical margin, and KRAS, TP53 or CDKN2A mutations.
source: The results of C-index indicated that AIDPS had significantly improved accuracy than these features, including age, gender, race, diabetic history, TNM stage, grade, primary location, history of radiotherapy or alcohol consumption, surgical margin, and KRAS, TP53 or CDKN2A mutations (Figure 2C–J).
evidence: Supported by C-index comparison shown in Figure 2C-J

claim: Only AIDPS and the 20-gene signature of Demirkol CS had consistent statistical significance in all 13 independent cohorts and Meta-Cohort among 86 published signatures.
source: The results of univariate Cox regression showed that only our AIDPS and 20-gene signature of Demirkol CS had consistent statistical significance in all 13 independent cohorts and Meta-Cohort (Figure 4A, Figure 3—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: Supported by univariate Cox regression analysis shown in Figure 4A

claim: AIDPS exhibited distinctly superior accuracy than other models in almost all cohorts (ranked first in four cohorts, ranked second in three cohorts, and ranked third in two cohorts).
source: Our AIDPS exhibited distinctly superior accuracy than the other models in almost all cohorts (ranked first in four cohorts, ranked second in three cohorts, and ranked third in two cohorts), revealing the robustness of AIDPS.
evidence: Supported by C-index comparison across multiple cohorts

claim: Patients with low AIDPS possessed more advanced grades.
source: However, patients with low AIDPS possessed more advanced grades, which might contribute to their worse prognosis (Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1M–P).
evidence: Supported by clinical characteristic comparison shown in Figure 5D

claim: The Kaplan–Meier survival curves exhibited significantly dismal OS for patients in the low AIDPS group in LIHC (p=0.016), STAD (p=0.037), COAD (p=0.032), and READ (p=0.026).
source: As shown in Figure 5E–H, the Kaplan–Meier survival curves exhibited significantly dismal OS for patients in the low AIDPS group in four tumors, including LIHC (p=0.016), STAD (p=0.037), COAD (p=0.032), and READ (p=0.026).
evidence: Supported by Kaplan-Meier analysis with specific p-values shown in Figure 5E-H

claim: The high AIDPS group was remarkably enriched for digestive and metabolism-related pathways, such as insulin secretion and regulation, peptide hormone secretion and regulation, fat digestion and absorption, pancreatic secretion, maturity onset diabetes of the young, and type Ⅱ diabetes mellitus.
source: As illustrated in Figure 5I and J, the high AIDPS group was remarkably enriched for digestive and metabolism-related pathways, such as insulin secretion and regulation, peptide hormone secretion and regulation, fat digestion and absorption, pancreatic secretion, maturity onset diabetes of the young, and type Ⅱ diabetes mellitus.
evidence: Supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5I and J

claim: The low AIDPS group was predominantly correlated with the regulation of T cell proliferation, IL-17 signaling pathway, and other immune-related pathways, as well as cell cycle, nuclear chromosome segregation, homologous recombination, and other proliferation-related biological processes.
source: While the low AIDPS group was predominantly correlated with the regulation of T cell proliferation, IL-17 signaling pathway, and other immune-related pathways, as well as cell cycle, nuclear chromosome segregation, homologous recombination, and other proliferation-related biological processes, which partly explained its more advanced grades and worse prognosis (Figure 5K and L).
evidence: Supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5K and L

claim: The low AIDPS group possessed observably higher tumor mutation burden (TMB).
source: As shown in Figure 6C, the low AIDPS group possessed observably higher tumor mutation burden (TMB).
evidence: Supported by TMB comparison shown in Figure 6C

claim: The classical tumor suppressor genes TP53, CDKN2A, and oncogene KRAS were more frequently mutated in the low AIDPS group than high AIDPS group.
source: Combining the 10 oncogenic signaling pathways in TCGA (Sanchez-Vega et al., 2018), we found that the classical tumor suppressor genes TP53, CDKN2A, and oncogene KRAS were more frequently mutated in the low AIDPS group than high AIDPS group, whereas the opposite was true for SMAD4, TTN, and RNF43 (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: Supported by mutation analysis shown in Figure 6A and B, with citation to Sanchez-Vega et al., 2018

claim: Mutational signature 3 (BRCA1/2 mutations-related) was enriched in the high AIDPS group, while mutational signature 1 (age-related) was more dominant in low AIDPS group.
source: Next, based on the popular mutational signatures in PACA, we discovered that mutational signature 3 (BRCA1/2 mutations-related) was enriched in the high AIDPS group, while mutational signature 1 (age-related) was more dominant in low AIDPS group.
evidence: Supported by mutational signature analysis

claim: The low AIDPS group owned evidently higher amplification or deletion in the focal and chromosome arm levels, such as the amplification of 8q24.21, 19q13.2, and 8p11.22 as well as deletion of 9p21.3, 18q21.2, 6p22.2, and 22q13.31.
source: Compared to the high AIDPS group, the low AIDPS group owned evidently higher amplification or deletion in the focal and chromosome arm levels, such as the amplification of 8q24.21, 19q13.2, and 8p11.22 as well as deletion of 9p21.3, 18q21.2, 6p22.2, and 22q13.31 (Figure 6A and D).
evidence: Supported by CNA analysis shown in Figure 6A and D

claim: Four methylation driver genes (MDGs) were screened whose methylation levels were significantly inversely related to matched gene expression levels in PACA.
source: Referring to our previous process (Liu et al., 2021b; Liu et al., 2021c), we screened four methylation driver genes (MDGs) whose methylation levels were significantly inversely related to matched gene expression levels in PACA.
evidence: Supported by methylation analysis with citations to Liu et al., 2021b and Liu et al., 2021c

claim: The high AIDPS group possessed higher MAP3K8 and PCDH7 methylation levels as well as significantly lower mRNA expression levels, while the opposite was true for PCDHB1 and SPAG6.
source: Compared to the low AIDPS group, the high AIDPS group possessed higher MAP3K8 and PCDH7 methylation levels as well as significantly lower mRNA expression levels, while the opposite was true for PCDHB1 and SPAG6 (Figure 6E and F).
evidence: Supported by methylation and expression analysis shown in Figure 6E and F

claim: Higher methylation levels of MAP3K8 and PCDH7 and lower methylation level of SPAG6 brought significantly prolonged OS for the high AIDPS group (all p<0.05).
source: Furthermore, the Kaplan–Meier analysis showed that higher methylation levels of MAP3K8 and PCDH7 and lower methylation level of SPAG6 brought significantly prolonged OS for the high AIDPS group (all p<0.05, Figure 6G, H and J).
evidence: Supported by Kaplan-Meier analysis shown in Figure 6G, H and J

claim: The low AIDPS group exhibited a relatively higher infiltration abundance of immune cell types, including activated CD4+ T cells, CD56dim natural killer cells, central memory CD8+ T cells, gamma delta T cells, and type 2T helper cells (all p<0.05).
source: According to single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA), we found that the low AIDPS group exhibited a relatively higher infiltration abundance of immune cell types, including activated CD4+ T cells, CD56dim natural killer cells, central memory CD8+ T cells, gamma delta T cells, and type 2T helper cells (all p<0.05, Figure 7A and B).
evidence: Supported by ssGSEA analysis shown in Figure 7A and B

claim: Among the 27 ICMs, the low AIDPS group had dramatically increased relative expression level, such as CD274, CD276, PDCD1LG2, CD40, CD70, TNFRSF18, TNFRSF4, TNFRSF9, and NT5E.
source: In addition, among the 27 ICMs we included, the low AIDPS group had dramatically increased relative expression level, such as CD274, CD276, PDCD1LG2, CD40, CD70, TNFRSF18, TNFRSF4, TNFRSF9, and NT5E (Figure 7C).
evidence: Supported by immune checkpoint molecule expression analysis shown in Figure 7C

claim: PACA patients with low AIDPS were more likely to respond to immunotherapy.
source: Together, these results consistently indicated that PACA patients with low AIDPS were more likely to respond to immunotherapy.
evidence: Inferred from immune landscape and ICM expression analysis

claim: The low AIDPS group resulted in significantly lower TIDE scores and higher immunotherapy response rates.
source: Based on the Tumour Immune Dysfunction and Exclusion (TIDE) web tool, the low AIDPS group resulted in significantly lower TIDE scores and higher immunotherapy response rates (Figure 8A and B).
evidence: Supported by TIDE analysis shown in Figure 8A and B

claim: Expression patterns of patients with low AIDPS was more similar to those of melanoma patients who responded to ICIs.
source: The results of the Subclass Mapping (Submap) also suggested that expression patterns of patients with low AIDPS was more similar to those of melanoma patients who responded to ICIs (Figure 8C).
evidence: Supported by Submap analysis shown in Figure 8C

claim: Four CTRP-derived agents (brefeldin A, oligomycin A, ouabain, and panobinostat) and nine PRISM-derived agents (aspirin, BAY-87–2243, EVP4593, GSK2656157, I-BET151, LY303511, OTX015, oxaliplatin, and XL388) were identified as potentially sensitive agents for the high AIDPS group.
source: Afterward, we applied this formula to identify potentially sensitive agents for the high AIDPS group, and finally generated four CTRP-derived agents (brefeldin A, oligomycin A, ouabain, and panobinostat) and nine PRISM-derived agents (aspirin, BAY-87–2243, EVP4593, GSK2656157, I-BET151, LY303511, OTX015, oxaliplatin, and XL388).
evidence: Supported by drug sensitivity analysis using CTRP and PRISM datasets

claim: Panobinostat with a –98.11 CMap score was highly sensitive in PACA patients, suggesting that it could become a potential therapeutic agent for PACA patients in the high AIDPS group.
source: Among them, panobinostat with a –98.11 CMap score was highly sensitive in PACA patients, suggesting that it could become a potential therapeutic agent for PACA patients in the high AIDPS group (Figure 8D).
evidence: Supported by CMap analysis shown in Figure 8D with speculative language ('suggesting', 'could become')

claim: Over the past 20 years, the incidence of PACA has increased by 0.5–1.0% per year, but the 5-year survival rate only improved from 5.26% to 10%, without a significant breakthrough.
source: Over the past 20 years, the incidence of PACA has increased by 0.5–1.0% per year, but the 5-year survival rate only improved from 5.26% to 10%, without a significant breakthrough (Park et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Park et al., 2021

claim: The study enrolled 1570 samples from 13 cohorts.
source: Finally, we enrolled 1570 samples from 13 cohorts, TCGA-PAAD (n = 176), ICGC-PACA-AU-Seq (PACA-AU-Seq, n = 81), ICGC-PACA-AU-Array (PACA-AU-Array, n = 267), ICGC-PACA-CA (PACA-CA-Seq, n = 182), E-MTAB-6134 (n = 288), GSE62452 (n = 65), GSE28735 (n = 42), GSE78229 (n = 49), GSE79668 (n = 51), GSE85916 (n = 79), GSE21501 (n = 102), GSE57495 (n = 63), and GSE71729 (n = 125).
evidence: Directly stated in Materials and methods with specific sample numbers for each cohort

claim: Consensus prognosis genes (CPGs) were selected based on the criteria: p<0.05 and all hazard ratios (HRs) consistently >1 or <1 in more than 8/10 cohorts.
source: We selected consensus prognosis genes (CPGs) for the next study according to the following criteria: p<0.05 and all hazard ratios (HRs) consistently >1 or <1 in more than 8/10 cohorts.
evidence: Directly stated in Materials and methods

claim: Ten classical algorithms were integrated: random forest (RSF), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), gradient boosting machine (GBM), survival support vector machine (Survival-SVM), supervised principal components (SuperPC), ridge regression, partial least squares regression for Cox (plsRcox), CoxBoost, Stepwise Cox, and elastic network (Enet).
source: First, we integrated 10 classical algorithms: random forest (RSF), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), gradient boosting machine (GBM), survival support vector machine (Survival-SVM), supervised principal components (SuperPC), ridge regression, partial least squares regression for Cox (plsRcox), CoxBoost, Stepwise Cox, and elastic network (Enet).
evidence: Directly stated in Materials and methods

claim: RSF, LASSO, CoxBoost, and Stepwise Cox have the function of dimensionality reduction and variable screening.
source: Among them, RSF, LASSO, CoxBoost, and Stepwise Cox have the function of dimensionality reduction and variable screening, and we combined them with other algorithms into 76 machine-learning algorithm combinations.
evidence: Directly stated in Materials and methods

claim: Elevated PAK1 activity was required for gemcitabine resistance in PACA, and PAK1 inhibition enhanced the efficacy of gemcitabine.
source: A laboratory study found that elevated PAK1 activity was required for gemcitabine resistance in PACA, and that PAK1 inhibition enhanced the efficacy of gemcitabine.
evidence: Stated as a finding from a laboratory study (though specific citation not provided in this sentence)

claim: Patients with low PAK1 expression possessed distinctly lower estimated AUC values, suggesting greater sensitivity to gemcitabine.
source: Consistent with this study, our results revealed that patients with low PAK1 expression possessed distinctly lower estimated AUC values, suggesting greater sensitivity to gemcitabine (Figure 8F).
evidence: Supported by drug sensitivity analysis shown in Figure 8F

claim: Amplification of 19q13.2 and consequent overexpression of this loci was correlated with impaired survival in PACA.
source: A recent study has shown that amplification of 19q13.2 and consequent overexpression of this loci was correlated with impaired survival in PACA (Sandhu et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sandhu et al., 2016

claim: Amplification of 8p11.22 was associated with chemotherapy resistance and shorter OS in ovarian clear cell carcinoma.
source: Morikawa et al., 2018 also found that amplification of 8p11.22 was associated with chemotherapy resistance and shorter OS in ovarian clear cell carcinoma.
evidence: Supported by citation to Morikawa et al., 2018

claim: People with 9p21.3 deletion were more susceptible to multiple types of tumors.
source: Baker et al., 2016 reviewed that people with 9p21.3 deletion were more susceptible to multiple types of tumors.
evidence: Supported by citation to Baker et al., 2016

claim: Deletion of 22q13.31 was an early genetic event in insulinoma independent of other genomic alteration and related to more advanced stage and dismal prognosis.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that deletion of 22q13.31 was an early genetic event in insulinoma independent of other genomic alteration and related to more advanced stage and dismal prognosis (Jonkers et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Jonkers et al., 2006

claim: Panobinostat can synergistically enhance the antitumor effect of the selective Wee1 kinase inhibitor MK-1775 or CAR-T cell therapy in PACA.
source: The latest studies report that panobinostat can synergistically enhance the antitumor effect of the selective Wee1 kinase inhibitor MK-1775 or CAR-T cell therapy in PACA (Wang et al., 2015; Ali et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wang et al., 2015 and Ali et al., 2021

claim: SELENBP1 with lower expression in the low AIDPS group was associated with better tumor prognosis, and its decreased expression led to poor prognosis of many tumors such as lung adenocarcinoma.
source: After careful literature research, we found that SELENBP1 that owned lower expression in the low AIDPS group with poor prognosis was associated with better tumor prognosis, and its decreased expression led to poor prognosis of many tumors such as lung adenocarcinoma (Chen et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2004

claim: PRR11, EREG, ADM, and TGM2, which were overexpressed in the low AIDPS group, played a vital role in the proliferation, invasion, and metastasis of many tumors such as breast cancer, colorectal cancer, and PACA, and lead to their chemotherapy resistance.
source: Meanwhile, PRR11, EREG, ADM, and TGM2, which were overexpressed in the low AIDPS group, played a vital role in the proliferation, invasion, and metastasis of many tumors such as breast cancer, colorectal cancer, and PACA, and lead to their chemotherapy resistance and were potential targets for enhanced efficacy (Lee et al., 2020; Neufert et al., 2013; Aggarwal et al., 2012; Malkomes et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lee et al., 2020; Neufert et al., 2013; Aggarwal et al., 2012; Malkomes et al., 2021

claim: There is no outstanding difference in age, gender, and TNM stage between high and low AIDPS groups.
source: We further compared several familiar clinical characteristics between the high and low AIDPS groups, and the results indicated the absence of statistical differences in age, gender, and TNM stage (Figure 5A–C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–L).
evidence: Supported by clinical characteristic comparison shown in Figure 5A-C

claim: The study constructed a nine-gene AIDPS.
source: After minimizing redundant information by CoxBoost, we finally obtained a nine-gene signature termed AIDPS through Survival-SVM.
evidence: Directly stated in the Discussion section

claim: The 20-gene signature of Demirkol CS, the 6-gene signature of Stratford JK, the 15-gene signature of Chen DT, and the 5-gene signature of Kim J were better than AIDPS in certain cohorts but were unsatisfactory across almost all validation cohorts.
source: It should be mentioned that, although the 20-gene signature of Demirkol CS, the 6-gene signature of Stratford JK, the 15-gene signature of Chen DT, and the 5-gene signature of Kim J, and so on were better than AIDPS in a certain cohort, but they were unsatisfactory across almost all validation cohorts, which might due to very poor generalization ability from overfitting.
evidence: Supported by comparison of C-index across multiple cohorts

claim: TP53, CDKN2A, and KRAS mutations promoted invasion, metastasis, and immune escape in PACA patients, resulting in worse prognosis.
source: Numerous studies have revealed that TP53, CDKN2A, and KRAS mutations promoted invasion, metastasis, and immune escape in PACA patients, resulting in worse prognosis (Hu et al., 2018; Hashimoto et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hu et al., 2018 and Hashimoto et al., 2019

claim: Relatively high-frequency genomic alteration and higher TMB provide more neoantigens, which might point the way for immunotherapy in the low AIDPS group.
source: On the other hand, relatively high-frequency genomic alteration and higher TMB also provide more neoantigens, which might point the way for immunotherapy in the low AIDPS group (Sha et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Sha et al., 2020 with speculative language ('might')

claim: Increased effector cells (activated CD4+ T cells, CD56dim natural killer cells, and central memory CD8+ T cells) will enhance antitumor immunity and bring better immunotherapeutic effects for the low AIDPS group.
source: As everyone knows, these increased effector cells will enhance antitumor immunity and bring better immunotherapeutic effects for the low AIDPS group (Borst et al., 2018; Wu et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Borst et al., 2018 and Wu et al., 2013

claim: The study screened 32 CPGs from 15,288 intersection genes in the training and nine testing cohorts.
source: Based on univariate Cox regression, we screened 32 CPGs from 15,288 intersection genes in the training and nine testing cohorts (Figure 2B).
evidence: Directly stated in Results section with reference to Figure 2B

claim: The high AIDPS group owned significantly prolonged OS in the three external validation cohorts (log-rank p=0.0014 in the GSE21501, 0.00045 in the GSE57495, 0.00011 in the GSE71729).
source: Kaplan–Meier survival analysis demonstrated that the high AIDPS group owned significantly prolonged OS in the three external validation cohorts (log-rank p=0.0014 in the GSE21501, 0.00045 in the GSE57495, 0.00011 in the GSE71729, Figure 3—figure supplement 4B–D).
evidence: Supported by Kaplan-Meier analysis with specific p-values

claim: The AUCs of 1-, 2-, and 3-year OS were 0.677, 0.681, and 0.761 in the GSE21501, 0.682, 0.728, and 0.747 in the GSE57495; 0.676, 0.693, and 0.714 in the GSE71729.
source: The AUCs of 1-, 2-, and 3-year OS were 0.677, 0.681, and 0.761 in the GSE21501, 0.682, 0.728, and 0.747 in the GSE57495; 0.676, 0.693, and 0.714 in the GSE71729 (Figure 3—figure supplement 4E–G).
evidence: Supported by ROC analysis with specific AUC values

claim: The vast majority of cohorts had good performance with a C-index greater than 0.65 for AIDPS.
source: Furthermore, although the 20-gene signature of Demirkol CS, the 3-gene signature of Chen H, the 6-gene signature of Hou J, the 7-gene signature of Liu X, and the 6-gene signature of Yu X_2 were superior to AIDPS in their training cohort or a few other cohorts, only our AIDPS possessed acceptable performance in all PACA cohorts, and the vast majority of cohorts had good performance with a C-index greater than 0.65 (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: Supported by C-index comparison shown in Figure 4B

claim: The model built by survival-SVM (the nine-gene AIDPS) achieved a maximum mean C-index of 0.666 in the remaining 12 multicenter cohorts among 18 models constructed via 10 common machine-learning algorithms.
source: As expected, among all 18 models, the model built by survival-SVM, namely, our nine-gene AIDPS, achieved a maximum mean C-index of 0.666 in the remaining 12 multicenter cohorts (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by C-index comparison shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D

claim: AIDPS brings significant performance improvements compared to the nine AIDPS genes alone.
source: Overall, our AIDPS brings significant performance improvements compared to the nine AIDPS genes alone.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of AIDPS with individual genes

claim: SELENBP1 and PLCB4, which were significantly positively correlated with AIDPS, had a moderate negative correlation with seven genes that were significantly negatively correlated with AIDPS in the whole and low AIDPS TCGA-PAAD.
source: The results showed that SELENBP1 and PLCB4, which were significantly positively correlated with AIDPS, had a moderate negative correlation with seven genes that were significantly negatively correlated with AIDPS in the whole and low AIDPS TCGA-PAAD (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A and C).
evidence: Supported by Pearson correlation analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A and C

claim: AIDPS and its positively correlated SELENBP1 and PLCB4 had a strong negative correlation with ICMs and immune cell types, while DCBLD2, PRR11, UNC13D, EREG, and TGM2, which were negatively correlated with AIDPS, were significantly positively correlated with ICMs and immune cell types in the whole and high AIDPS TCGA-PAAD.
source: The Pearson correlation analysis exhibited that AIDPS and its positively correlated SELENBP1 and PLCB4 had a strong negative correlation with ICMs and immune cell types, while DCBLD2, PRR11, UNC13D, EREG, and TGM2, which were negatively correlated with AIDPS, were significantly positively correlated with ICMs and immune cell types in the whole and high AIDPS TCGA-PAAD (Figure 7—figure supplement 2D, E, G, H).
evidence: Supported by Pearson correlation analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2D, E, G, H

claim: SELENBP1 and PLCB4, which were positively correlated with AIDPS, were significantly lower in the low AIDPS group with superior mutation and CNA frequency, suggesting that they were significantly negatively correlated with TMB and CNA burden.
source: In terms of genomic alteration, we also observed that SELENBP1 and PLCB4, which were positively correlated with AIDPS, were significantly lower in the low AIDPS group with superior mutation and CNA frequency, suggesting that they were significantly negatively correlated with TMB and CNA burden (Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by genomic alteration analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3

claim: DCBLD2, PRR11, UNC13D, EREG, ADM, CDCA4, and TGM2, which were negatively correlated with AIDPS, were remarkably increased in the low AIDPS group, hinting they were significantly positively correlated with TMB and CNA burden.
source: Correspondingly, DCBLD2, PRR11, UNC13D, EREG, ADM, CDCA4, and TGM2, which were negatively correlated with AIDPS, were remarkably increased in the low AIDPS group, hinting they were significantly positively correlated with TMB and CNA burden (e.g., the low AIDPS group possessed higher TP53 mutation and 8q24.21 amplification, as well as higher DCBLD2 expression, Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by genomic alteration analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3
